issues.detail: The Hebrew 'נַשְׁקֶנּוּ יַיִן' means 'let us make him drink wine' (give him wine to drink). The Chinese '用酒類使他喝醉' adds '使他喝醉' (make him drunk), which is an interpretive addition; the Hebrew only says 'make him drink wine' without explicitly stating the purpose of drunkenness in this clause.
